subject: SLO Targeting: end-to-end tail latency & streaming handshake (hosted vs incumbent)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLO Targeting: end-to-end tail latency & streaming handshake (hosted vs incumbent)

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on the business priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the performance asks and what we’ll run in the PoC.

Key context (from the call)
- Brightline is highly latency-sensitive for user-facing features (search/autocomplete + live chat).
- Current provider meets throughput but the tail is causing UX regressions at peak traffic.
- You asked us to validate: end-to-end p95/p99 (client-perceived), sustained throughput/QPS, concurrency envelope for streaming sessions, and streaming chunk latency.

What we propose to measure (PoC scope)
1) Non-streaming (request/response) e2e: measure p50/p95/p99 including client network + edge.
2) Streaming (chunked tokens): measure first-chunk latency and per-chunk tail (p95/p99) under concurrent streams.
3) Throughput & concurrency profile: sustained QPS baseline + 30% burst window; max concurrent streaming sessions target.
4) Reproduction using two traffic sources: (a) synthetic injector in us-west-2, (b) replay of anonymized production traces you supply (sample).

Initial acceptance targets (for discussion)
- Non-streaming: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 900ms (client-perceived).
- Streaming: first-chunk p95 <= 400ms, streaming-chunk p95 <= 500ms, p99 <= 1.2s.
- Sustained throughput: 100 QPS with 30% burst to 130 QPS for 5 minutes without tail degradation.
- Concurrent streams: support 60 concurrent streams in the streaming model (stable tails).

What we need from Brightline to run the PoC
- A sample of anonymized production traces (request + timestamps, header shapes) — see attached probe template.
- A small allowlist for our probe IPs and for streaming ingress endpoints.
- Confirmation of the primary region (us-west preferred) and an example client (web/SDK) path you want included.

Attachments: SLO-Probe-Config.yaml (probe template), Brightline-MAP-v2.pdf (mutual action plan we discussed).

Next steps
1) You confirm the acceptance targets above or propose adjustments (reply here).
2) Brightline shares sample traces and allowlist.
3) Redwood schedules a 3-day PoC (two traffic sources + ramp). Post-run we’ll share raw traces and a breakdown (edge, runtime, queuing).

Thanks — I’ll hold a calendar slot for Wed-Thu next week for the PoC kickoff (confirm preferred timezone).

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightline.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@brightline.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLO Targeting: end-to-end tail latency & streaming handshake (hosted vs incumbent)

Jordan — thanks for the concise recap. Good to see the proposed test surface; a few clarifications and numbers from our side: 

Current observed baselines (incumbent provider, US west, median of last 7 days):
- Non-streaming: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.8s (these include our client SDK network overhead).
- Streaming (web SDK, chunking every 120 tokens): first-chunk p95 ~ 600ms, chunk p99 up to 2.2s under peak.
- Typical sustained QPS: 60–80 across peak hour; instantaneous bursts to ~140 QPS during promo spikes.
- Concurrent streams observed: peaks at ~40 simultaneous long-lived chat streams during peak.

Acceptance target: our internal bar is tighter than current provider; ideally we want to land at or under p95 300ms and p99 800ms for non-streaming, but we are realistic and willing to evaluate Redwood’s measured numbers if they include client-perceived time. For streaming, first-chunk p95 <= 450ms would be a big improvement.

On deliverables: we can produce an anonymized sample trace (I’ll route to engineering). We’ll also provide an allowlist for probing. We’ll need to confirm whether Redwood’s measurements count CDN edge or measure from our client agent — please call that out in the runbook.

I’ll coordinate with Elena to push the traces; expect them by EOD Monday.

—
Tom Alvarez
Head of Product, Brightline AI
tom.alvarez@brightline.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightline.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLO Targeting: end-to-end tail latency & streaming handshake (hosted vs incumbent)

Tom — great numbers, and thanks for the quick turnaround on traces. A few clarifications from an engineering/runbook perspective so expectations are aligned: 

Measurement boundaries
- Redwood’s default PoC measurement is "client-perceived" end-to-end: we instrument a light client (same SDK call pattern you use) running in us-west-2 to include network egress + edge handoff + runtime.
- We will also report a breakdown: network & ingress (~edge), queuing/dispatch, runtime token generation, and response serialization.

Test plan highlights
- Synthetic injector: will hammer controlled QPS profiles (baseline, 30% burst, 3-minute soak).
- Trace replay: we’ll replay anonymized requests at the original inter-arrival times where possible to see real-world tail behavior.
- Streaming specifics: two scenarios — (A) short-lived streams (single prompt -> short multi-chunk reply), (B) long-lived interactive streams (hour-ish sessions with frequent server-sent chunks). We’ll instrument first-chunk and chunk-to-chunk intervals.

Acceptance definition (proposed conservative window for PoC)
- Non-streaming: p95 <= 380ms, p99 <= 1.0s — we ask Brightline to accept these as the PoC gate because they include client network variance.
- Streaming: first-chunk p95 <= 480ms, chunk p95 <= 600ms, chunk p99 <= 1.3s.

If you prefer we can tighten to Tom’s aspirational numbers for the contract phase, but for the PoC we want a realistic band that accounts for client network variance.

Operational asks
- Please provide: (1) small trace sample, (2) allowlist for these probe IPs (we’ll send), (3) expected SDK/headers we should mirror.
- Confirm the region for the PoC: us-west-2.

I’ll attach the probe template (SLO-Probe-Config.yaml) — use it to format the trace export. Once we have traces and allowlist we’ll schedule the PoC and share a detailed runbook and an evaluation sheet.

Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 12:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLO Targeting: end-to-end tail latency & streaming handshake (hosted vs incumbent)

Perfect — thanks both. Action items and timeline below: 

Action items
1) Brightline (Tom/Elena): share anonymized trace sample + confirm allowlist by EOD Mon (Feb 22).
2) Redwood (Marissa/Priyom/Jordan): finalize probe config and send probe IPs + runbook by Tue (Feb 23).
3) PoC window: Wed–Fri next week (Feb 24–26), synthetic + trace replay. Results report by end-of-day Mon (Mar 1).

Decision criteria post-PoC
- We’ll deliver a per-route breakdown with client-perceived p95/p99 and components. If Redwood meets the PoC acceptance band above we’ll document the exact SLOs for the contract (Tom’s aspirational numbers are a useful reference).

Scheduling: I’ll hold the kickoff slot Wed 09:00 PT; please confirm or propose an alternate.

Thanks again — attaching the MAP we discussed (Brightline-MAP-v2.pdf).

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
